source.title: Scaling Laws for the Few-Shot Adaptation of Pre-trained Image Classifiers
source.authors: Gabriele Prato; Simon Guiroy; Ethan Caballero; I. Rish; A. P. Sarath Chandar

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and figures are flattened in the web text, but the relevant ImageNet fit constants are also given in Table 1.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling in image-classification and few-shot adaptation, a modality and evaluation setting beyond text pretraining; it reports performance as training-data size changes.
record.gate_note: The study measures few-shot image-classification error while scaling training examples and classes. Table 1 gives fitted one-shot error curves for ImageNet-trained models, averaged over target datasets. Results cited from other papers in Related Work are not recorded as rows. Most per-dataset results appear only in figures and are not enumerated individually here.
record.test_reason: It scales the pretraining set size of image classifiers (6.25% to 100%) and fits power laws with an irreducible-error term to few-shot transfer error on new classes. That bears on V5, the power-law form holding beyond text pretraining in a transfer setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Scaling training-set size generally improves few-shot performance on new image classes and is well approximated by power laws, for same-domain and different-domain targets, with exceptions (CNN, Traffic Sign). Few-shot performance converges faster than in-distribution classification.
record.recipe_differences: Scales image-classifier training examples and classes, measuring few-shot classification error or accuracy rather than held-out language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with architecture, few-shot evaluation method, source and target datasets, and whether training examples or training classes are scaled; the paper reports weaker or absent gains in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling the number of training classes at fixed data: no average gain for Fungi or Omniglot, gains leveling off after about 200 classes for ImageNet, steady gains for COCO (64 classes).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-shot transfer performance improves with the number of pretraining classes only up to a plateau.

record.problems: For the relevant results, uncertainty estimates are not reported. Most dataset-specific outcomes are shown in plots rather than tabulated, and the fitted curves concern few-shot error on images rather than language-model held-out loss.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional train-target dataset, architecture, and shot-count combinations in Figures 3–17 and Appendix A.2. These were not recorded individually; the main text's explicit aggregate exceptions and the ImageNet one-shot fits are retained.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured.
No extrapolation test is made; fits are on in-range points only.
Architectures differ in size and family; shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
Model size and compute are not scaled. The data range is only 16x, not several orders of magnitude. Other modalities (video), repeated data and full fine-tuning are not tested.
No language-model downstream tasks, and no prediction from pretraining loss.
Fitting choices are not examined. Exponents vary by model and evaluation method (-0.25 to -1.06), but this is not analysed.

missing.what: With Traffic Sign as the training dataset, scaling data does not improve few-shot performance on average.
Scaling Omniglot training data gives little gain on other targets; scaling natural-image sources improves Omniglot and other natural targets.
Few-shot performance on new classes converges faster than in-distribution ImageNet test performance as data scales.
5-shot and per-source results for COCO, Fungi and ImageNet (plots only).

record.verdict_notes: V6 links were removed: V6 concerns language-model downstream performance, and image transfer falls under V5. The power-law evidence is thin: 5 data points over 1.2 orders of magnitude, with no fit quality or uncertainty reported. Class-count rows were moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure held-out language-model pretraining loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Does not test whether fits on smaller runs predict much larger runs.
Does not compare parameter and token allocations at fixed compute.
Compares image-classifier architectures, but does not hold parameter count fixed while varying depth, width, or other architecture details.

Tests image-classification few-shot performance as training examples and training classes scale. Does not test video, repeated-data training, fine-tuning or transfer regimes beyond its stated few-shot evaluation.
Tests few-shot image-classification performance as training-data size changes; does not test language-model downstream tasks or predict performance from pretraining loss.
Does not test whether language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on fitting choices, nor whether language-model loss curves bend.
